draft.title: Evidence for the big bang
card: Light from distant galaxies is stretched to longer wavelengths, which moves it towards the red end of the spectrum. This is called redshift.
Redshift shows that these galaxies are moving away from us. The more distant a galaxy is, the greater its redshift, so the more distant galaxies are moving away faster.
If galaxies are moving apart now, then in the past they were closer together. This fits a universe that began in a hot, dense state and has been expanding.

Faint microwave radiation, called cosmic microwave background radiation, reaches Earth from every direction in space. It is the leftover glow from the early universe, and the big bang theory predicted it.
draft.remember: Redshift shows galaxies moving apart. Microwave background radiation is leftover glow from the early universe.

a.q: Astronomers find that light from a distant galaxy is redshifted. What does this show about the galaxy?
opts: It is moving away from us
It is made of different elements
It is a very young galaxy
a.why: Redshift means the light has been stretched to longer wavelengths, which happens when a galaxy moves away from us. Moving towards us would not stretch the light towards red.
a.clue: Think about what stretching the light tells you about the galaxy's motion.

b.q: Astronomers measure two galaxies. Galaxy P has a small redshift and galaxy Q has a much larger redshift. What can they conclude?
opts: Q is more distant and moving away faster
Q is closer and moving away more slowly
P is more distant and moving away faster
P and Q are the same distance from us
b.why: A greater redshift goes with a greater distance and a faster speed away from us. Q has the larger redshift, so it is further away and moving away faster. Reading a larger redshift as a closer galaxy reverses the pattern.
b.clue: The more distant a galaxy is, the greater its redshift.

a.best: It is moving away from us

b.best: Q is more distant and moving away faster
